newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: MOTOR RACING-VILLENEUVE TAKES ARGENTINE POLE SPOT.
newsitem.headline: MOTOR RACING-VILLENEUVE TAKES ARGENTINE POLE SPOT.

text.p: Jacques Villeneuve continued his dominance of this year's Formula One world championship on Saturday, winning pole position for Sunday's Argentine Grand Prix.
The Canadian shattered the old qualifying record by more than six seconds by lapping in one minute 24.473 seconds in his Williams-Renault.
Still suffering from a stomach disorder, Villeneuve said the extra performance of the car was down to the vastly improved tyres this season.
"Last year, they were too hard on this circuit and this year they are much better, much softer," he explained.
His team mate Heinz-Harald Frentzen wound up second-quickest to claim a place alongside the Canadian on the front row of the grid.
It was Villeneuve's third pole position of the season, his fourth in succession, the sixth of his career -- and the 100th for Williams.
The 26-year-old shares the lead in the world drivers' championship with Briton David Coulthard with 10 points after two of the 17 races on the calendar.

Frenchman Olivier Panis in a Prost, using the new Bridgestone tyres as opposed to the Goodyears of the Williams team, claimed third place ahead of double world champion Michael Schumacher of Germany in a Goodyear-shod Ferrari.

Rubens Barrichello, in a Jordan with Bridgestone tyres, was fifth and Ralf Schumacher, 21-year-old younger brother of Michael, was sixth for Jordan, using Goodyears, as they qualified for their 100th Grand Prix.
The race will be the 600th Formula One world championship event since the series was inaugurated in 1950.

Panis' third place was his best-ever qualifying position and Barrichello claimed the Stewart team's first top 10 starting place on the grid. Britain's Damon Hill, the 1996 world champion, qualified 13th for Arrows.
"It was difficult for me because we never had a set-up from the morning session when I had a radiator problem, so we were guessing as we qualified," Hill said.
"I thought we would be doing well to get in the top 10 here, so 13 is not too bad. I think we did the best we could under the circumstances."
There are reports that Arrows are to have a new car powered by Honda next year.
For Barrichello, it was a profitable as well as an invigorating afternoon. Returning to the Stewart team's garage, he tossed his wrist-watch out of the cockpit of his car.
The Brazilian had won a bet with team bosses Jackie and Paul Stewart -- for finishing in the top six for the first time -- and won a new watch.
Jackie Stewart said: "This is fantastic. To qualify in the top six for the first time after translating our second position in Friday's practice to fifth on the grid is wonderful."
